author: Anastasy sweet

title: It is a super app, but there are too few categories (only 12)
body:
I absolutely love this app. It combines features of a to-do list with that of a done list, and can help manage habit stacks, not just individual habits. 

I have been looking for something like this for, literally, years. 

The app has an intuitive minimalistic interface. And it is super easy to use once you have sorted out what you need to get done into categories or habit stacks. It lets you choose an icon for each habit (stack), so all you life is literally summarised pictorially if you have taken your time to categorise everything (I have spent about two hours). 

I hope that in the future it will be possible either to add more sets of 6 tasks/habits/habit (stacks), or to give each habit (stack) a much longer description, specifying how many times and how often you should do each task or in which order the tasks should be done within each category. Or both. 

For example, I would like to go outside every day. To make it more productive, I specify the number of steps I have to make, the number of pics to take (I usually create a blog entry with the pics, so the whole thing is more fun: it was difficult to think of a good reason to go out when I worked from home, so now I have something to look forward to). But on some days I have more time. On those days I go on longer walks and listen to audiobooks. So this whole thing is one complex habit stack. It would be great if it were possible to add its description as a single habit (stack) or category, one if the six in a set, and not break it down into smaller ones. 

Thank you for the great app! I will recommend it to all my friends.
